The strategy will focus on identifying stocks with a higher relative strength index (RSI) compared to the broader market universe. The RSI measures the magnitude of recent price changes to evaluate overbought or oversold conditions. By selecting stocks that outperform their peers, we aim to capture alpha.

This phenomenon might persist due to factors such as investor sentiment, company-specific news, and liquidity. Strong firms with positive fundamental changes can attract more attention, driving up their relative strength compared to the broader market, even if overall market performance is weak.

The trading rule would involve selecting the top N% of stocks by RSI relative to the BSE Sensex or NIFTY 50 index. These selected stocks would then be weighted based on their relative RSI for portfolio construction. This approach aims to benefit from overbought conditions in high-quality stocks, potentially offering excess returns.

The signal for this systematic equity strategy involves computing the Relative Strength Index (RSI) for each stock in the BSE Sensex or NIFTY 50 index. The RSI is calculated based on daily open, high, low, close prices over a lookback period of 14 days. On any given day, stocks are ranked by their RSI relative to the broader market index. The top N% of stocks with the highest RSIs are selected and weighted according to their RSI values for portfolio construction. This ranking helps identify stocks that have outperformed recently, potentially benefiting from overbought conditions in high-quality stocks.

The strategy will hold positions in the top N% of stocks by RSI relative to the BSE Sensex or NIFTY 50 index. Positions are weighted based on each stock's RSI value to emphasize higher quality stocks. To manage risk, a maximum portfolio loss limit of ±10% per month is set. This limits the overall exposure and helps ensure that no single stock can significantly impact the portfolio's performance, promoting a balanced approach to capital preservation and return enhancement.
